title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'formulaire' that identifies the 'cartographic' group of type (0,3) with the modular group. On the previous page Grothendieck set up isomorphisms C_{0,3} ≅ GL(2,Z)/±1 = PGL(2,Z) and C^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)/±1 = PSL(2,Z), sending σ_∞ ↦ [[0,-1],[1,0]] (order 2) and ρ ↦ [[0,1],[-1,1]] (order 3).

The page then does the following.

(43) It records the inverse formula u^{-1} = [[d,-b],[-c,a]] for u in SL(2,Z). A marginal N.B. generalises this: det(u)·u^{-1} = adj(u) for u in GL(2,A), A any ring.

(44) It defines three elements ε_0 = σ_∞ρ, ε_1 = ρσ_∞ and ε_∞ = ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ^{-1}, together with their inverses. Their squares are ℓ_0 = [[1,-2],[0,1]], ℓ_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]] and ℓ_∞ = [[3,-2],[2,-1]]. It also lists the three involutions σ_0 = [[1,-1],[2,-1]], σ_1 = [[1,-2],[1,-1]] and σ_∞. One checks σ_0 = ρσ_∞ρ^{-1} and σ_1 = ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ, so these are the three conjugate order-2 elements attached to the three cusps 0, 1, ∞.

(45) It gives ρ and ρ^{-1}.

(46) It computes ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = -I in SL(2,Z). This is the nontrivial central element, which 'heureusement' becomes 1 in PSL(2,Z). There it yields the defining relation ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1 of π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}).

(47)/(48) The exact sequence 1 → π_{0,3} → C^+_{0,3} → Γ^+_{0,3} ≅ S_3 → 1 is identified with 1 → Γ(2)/±1 → PSL(2,Z) → SL(2,F_2) ≅ S_3 → 1. Here π(2)' = Γ(2)/±1 is free on ℓ_0 and ℓ_1, i.e. it is π_{0,3}.

The ε_i are square roots in PSL(2,Z) of the loop generators ℓ_i. Each maps to a transposition in S_3 (it is the lift over a cusp), as do the σ_i. Geometrically this is the classical fact that the modular curve X(2) (λ-line) is P^1 - {0,1,∞}, with PSL(2,Z)/Γ(2) = S_3 acting by the anharmonic group. The next page notes that the central extension SL(2,Z) is T_{1,1}, the mapping class group of the once-punctured torus. The purpose is a dictionary for the 'équation des lacets' and Galois–Teichmüller work in genus 0 with 3 and 4 points.
errors: The product ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ^{-1} actually equals [[-2,1],[-1,0]] = -[[2,-1],[1,0]]. The written ε_∞ is thus correct only in PSL(2,Z) (mod ±1), which is the group in which Grothendieck says he identifies elements. Similarly, ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = -I shows the chosen matrix lifts satisfy the loop relation only up to sign. This sign subtlety is exactly what the 'heureusement!' remark addresses. On the previous page he even notes 'il vaut mieux changer les signes'.
All other matrices check: ε_0, ε_1, their inverses, ε_∞^{-1}, ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞, σ_0, σ_1, ρ^{±1}, and the product in (46).

ideas.what: Identification of the oriented cartographic group of type (0,3) with PSL(2,Z), and of π_{0,3} with the principal congruence subgroup Γ(2)/±1 (free on [[1,2],[0,1]] and [[1,0],[2,1]]), with quotient SL(2,F_2) ≅ S_3
ideas.modern_name: X(2) = P^1 - {0,1,∞}; Γ(2)/±1 ≅ F_2; anharmonic group S_3 = PSL(2,Z)/Γ(2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke, Sanov 1949 for freeness of Γ(2)); in the dessins setting, Grothendieck and later Jones–Singerman and Malgoire–Voisin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups as finite-index-related to PSL/PGL(2,Z), Γ(2) and the λ-line); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Lifting the loop relation ℓ_∞ℓ_1ℓ_0 = 1 to SL(2,Z) gives -I, the central element; SL(2,Z) as central extension related to T_{1,1}
ideas.modern_name: SL(2,Z) ≅ mapping class group of the once-punctured torus (Γ_{1,1}); B_3/center relation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Γ_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) in the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Square roots ε_i of the loop generators and the conjugate involutions σ_i attached to the three cusps
ideas.modern_name: Parabolic elements of PSL(2,Z) at cusps of X(2); elliptic involutions

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an explicit matrix dictionary for the classical identification PSL(2,Z)/Γ(2) ≅ S_3 with Γ(2)/±1 ≅ π_1(P^1 - 3 points). All computations are routine and standard in the literature, and the framework already appears in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: The ε_∞ formula reads ρ^{-1}σ_∞ρ^{-1} in the image. The stated matrix [[2,-1],[1,0]] equals the actual product only up to sign.
Under π(2)' in (48) the image shows π_{0,3} with an extra superscript or decoration ('≃' sign and possibly a 'δ'-like mark), which is hard to read.
The page number at top is uncertain: it could be 338 or 335.
